property_summary: A Put call that would cause overflow with a large msg.value reverts in P but succeeds in M.
After any call to Put, the caller's balance in Acc must equal the total Ether sent by that caller through Put; the buggy subtraction violates this invariant.

After any call to Put, the caller's unlockTime in Acc must be at least block.timestamp; the buggy subtraction can cause a revert in Collect when block.timestamp > unlockTime due to balance becoming negative, violating the invariant that Put always succeeds.

After a successful call to Put with any msg.value, the contract's ETH balance must increase by exactly msg.value; in the buggy version, balance subtraction breaks this invariant by decreasing the contract's balance instead.
After any successful call to Put, the caller's balance in Acc must be at least msg.value; the buggy subtraction can make it lower, violating this invariant.

For any sequence of Put calls, the sum of Acc balances over all callers must equal the contract's ETH balance plus the total locked MinSum claims that have been collected; the buggy subtraction breaks this conservation invariant.

For any user, calling Put with some msg.value and then calling Put again with a different msg.value should result in a balance equal to the sum of both values, but the buggy addition causes the balance to be overwritten with the second value instead of adding it.
After two consecutive Put calls by the same sender with different values and unlock times, the final balance must equal the sum of both msg.values, but the bug overwrites with the second value.

After two Put calls by the same sender where the second call carries a different msg.value, the resulting balance must not equal the second msg.value alone, but the bug overwrites instead of adding, so the balance equals the second msg.value.
For any sender, after two Put calls with the same unlock time, the balance must equal the sum of both msg.values, but the bug overwrites the balance with the second msg.value instead of adding.

After any sequence of Put calls from the same sender, the contract's balance must equal the sum of all received msg.values, but the bug overwrites balance with the last msg.value, causing the contract's balance to be less than the cumulative sum.

After any sequence of Put calls, the sum of all msg.value sent must equal the total Acc balances tracked; the buggy version omits balance updates causing Acc balances to remain zero despite received Ether.
After a Put call, the Acc balance of the caller must be at least the msg.value sent, which the buggy version violates because it never increments the balance.

After a successful Collect call, the caller's Acc balance must be strictly less than before the call; the buggy version never increments balance on Put, causing Collect to revert if the balance is zero, but the rule tracks balance reduction on successful Collect, which the reference satisfies and the buggy version can be made to fail when an existing balance is drained.

For any address that has called Put with msg.value > 0, the Acc balance of that address must equal the sum of all msg.value sent in its Put calls, which the buggy version violates by never incrementing acc.balance.

For any address that has called Put with a non-zero msg.value, a subsequent Collect of an amount >0 must succeed (not revert) if balance, unlockTime, and timestamp conditions are met; the buggy version never increments the balance, so such a Collect always reverts.
The sum of Acc[msg.sender].balance after Put should never be less than its balance before Put; the buggy version can overflow, making the final balance smaller than the initial balance.

After a call to Put(...), the sum of all Acc[...].balance values across all addresses is at least the sum of all msg.value sent through Put. The buggy version can overflow acc.balance, causing the total balance sum to be less than expected.
After Put, the caller's Acc balance is at least the msg.value sent; the buggy version overflows so the post‑balance can be zero or less than msg.value.

After any Put call by a sender with a non-zero existing balance, the sender's total balance (Acc balance) must be strictly greater than the msg.value sent (since pre-balance > 0), but the buggy overflow allows the final balance to be less than or equal to msg.value.
After Put, the caller's balance is always at least their previous balance; the buggy version can overflow, making the new balance strictly less than the old balance.
After any call to Put, the unlockTime for msg.sender must be >= block.timestamp; the mutant sets it to 0, violating this when block.timestamp > 0.
After any successful call to Put, the unlockTime for the caller must be strictly greater than 0; the mutant sets it to 0, violating this for any input.

For every successful call to Put, the caller's unlockTime after the call must be either the provided _unlockTime if it is in the future, or block.timestamp if _unlockTime is not in the future; the mutant always sets unlockTime to 0, violating this when the caller does a Put with _unlockTime in the past and block.timestamp > 0.

After a successful call to Put, the caller's unlockTime must be greater than the block timestamp at the time of the previous Put call. The mutant sets unlockTime to 0, violating this when block.timestamp is non-zero.
After any call to Put, the caller's unlockTime must be at least block.timestamp; the mutant sets it to 0, which is less than block.timestamp whenever block.timestamp > 0, violating the rule.
After any call to Put, the stored unlockTime is never less than block.timestamp; the mutant storing the raw _unlockTime can set unlockTime in the past.

After a call to Put, the stored unlockTime is at least as large as the input _unlockTime when _unlockTime is in the future; the mutant can set unlockTime to any past value, breaking the invariant that unlockTime >= _unlockTime for future timestamps.
After any call to Put, the stored unlockTime must be greater than or equal to block.timestamp; the mutant can set unlockTime to any value, including one strictly less than block.timestamp.
After any Put, the stored unlockTime is at least block.timestamp; the mutant loses the floor, so an _unlockTime in the past leaves unlockTime < block.timestamp.

For any address that has only called Put with a non-zero msg.value, the unlockTime stored in Acc[address] can never be strictly less than the block.timestamp at which Put was last called; the buggy version allows this when _unlockTime is in the past.
After any call to Put, the latest History entry must have Sender equal to the caller; the mutant logs address(0), so a non-zero caller violates this.
After sending any ETH via fallback or calling Put, the Sender logged in History must match the original msg.sender; the mutant logs address(0), violating this for any non-zero sender.
For any call to Put, the last entry in the Log's History must have Sender equal to the caller; the mutant logs address(0), so with a non-zero caller the recorded sender mismatches.
After any call to Put, the LastMsg.Sender of the LogFile must match the original msg.sender; the mutant logs address(0), so for any non-zero caller it breaks this invariant.
Collect only succeeds when a pending Put has previously set an unlock time that has already passed.
Collect reverts unless a prior Put set an unlock time that has already passed.
If Collect reverts, then block.timestamp must be less than or equal to _unlockTime.
If a Collect after a Put reverts, then block.timestamp must be <= the unlock time set by that Put.
If Collect reverts, then block.timestamp must be less than or equal to the unlock time set by Put.

The correct contract only allows Collect when block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime, so a successful Collect implies timestamp > unlockTime; the buggy version allows Collect before unlock, violating that invariant.
After any call to Collect, the caller's balance must never decrease when block.timestamp <= their unlockTime; the mutant allows a decrease in that state.
After any call to Collect, if block.timestamp <= acc[caller].unlockTime, the caller's balance must remain unchanged; the buggy version decreases it.
When block.timestamp is before a depositor's unlockTime, their collected amount must always be zero, but the mutant allows collection before unlock.

A call to Collect that transfers Ether to an external address only succeeds (does not revert) if the caller's unlockTime has passed; the mutant succeeds before the unlock, causing a transfer that should revert.
Collect can only succeed when the caller's balance is at least MinSum
Collect must revert when the caller's balance is below MinSum.
